subject: science
title: Force and Earth Words
about: The science words from NC's forces, sky and Earth-materials standards, as 'what do we call' cards. These are the words the teacher uses, so hearing them often makes class easier.
tip: After he taps the word, ask him to use it in a sentence about something in the room.

cards.q: What do we call a push or a pull?
cards.note: A kick is a push. Opening a drawer is a pull. Both are forces.

cards.q: What do we call it when something moves?
cards.note: A rolling car is in motion. A push or pull can start it, stop it or turn it.

cards.q: What do we call a thing that pulls some metals without touching them?
cards.note: A magnet can pull a paper clip without touching it. It pulls some metals, not all.

cards.q: What do we call a test to find an answer?
cards.note: Say in-ves-ti-GAY-shun. Pushing a toy car softly and then hard is an investigation.

cards.q: What do we call what we see and write down in a test?
cards.note: How far the car rolled each time is data.

cards.q: What do we call telling how two things are alike and different?
cards.note: We compare a soft push and a hard push to see what changed.

cards.q: What do we call something that happens again and again?
cards.note: Day, then night, then day again is a pattern.

cards.q: What do we call the star that gives us light and heat?
cards.note: The sun is a star. Never look right at it.

cards.q: What do we call a far-away ball of light in the night sky?
cards.note: Stars look tiny because they are so far away.

cards.q: What do we call a smart guess about what comes next?
cards.note: Say pre-DIK-shun. If you know the pattern, you can make a prediction.

cards.q: What do we call the bits that rocks are made of?
cards.note: Look closely at a rock. The little specks and sparkles are minerals.

cards.q: What do we call something that keeps its shape, like a rock?
cards.note: A rock stays a rock in a cup, in a box or in your hand.

cards.q: What do we call something that flows and takes the shape of its cup?
cards.note: Water in a cup is a liquid. Pour it in a bowl and it takes the shape of the bowl.

cards.q: What do we call how something feels?
cards.note: Rough, smooth, bumpy and soft are all textures.

cards.q: What do we call something you can observe about a thing, like its color?
cards.note: Color, size, shape and texture are properties of a rock.

cards.q: What do we call the top layer of ground where plants grow?
cards.note: Soil is not all the same. Some is sandy and some is sticky.

cards.q: What do we call the things in soil that help plants grow?
cards.note: Say NOO-tree-unts. Good soil gives plants water and nutrients.

cards.q: What do we call the dark part of soil made from rotted plants?
cards.note: Say HYOO-mus. Old leaves rot and turn into humus.
